$comment: ADR-020 D1 made mechanical for the service_case schema — GEN-038. NOT a contract file: cut A ships no endpoint, so this scans SCHEMA COLUMN NAMES, COLUMN TYPES and seed values rather than a response corpus. DERIVED BY DIFFING tests/integration/interest-forbidden-terms.json (ADR-011 D5, API-027-ST's method), with every decision recorded in diffDecisions.
purpose: PEMO is the system of record for the CASE and a CONSUMER of the work order (ADR-020 D1). A column named for a technician, a part, a labour line, a cost or a crew schedule is a defect, because that is precisely the thing PEMO does not hold.
theInversion: The interest list moved the money family IN because PEMO holds the relationship, never the instrument. This list KEEPS that and adds the WORK-EXECUTION family for the same reason one layer out: PEMO holds that work happened, never how it was done. It also scans TYPES, which no earlier list did.

money.reason: Any monetary amount or charge. D1: if a fact would change when the money changes, it is not PEMO's.

secrets.reason: Universal, kept verbatim from all three lists. No credential in any row.

work_execution.reason: ADR-020 D1: PEMO records THAT a job exists in another system and what that system last said. The moment a column names who did the work, what it consumed, or when the crew is coming, PEMO has started to MODEL the work — and the pressure to add 'just the cost' arrives with the first report anybody asks for.

monetary_type.reason: The dispatch requires 'any monetary type', not only a monetary NAME. A column called `adjustment numeric(12,2)` carries money while dodging every name-based term, so this denylist scans DATA TYPES too — the first thing this list does that the interest's did not.

allowedExceptions.reason: external_ref and display_ref are references TO other systems, which is exactly what D1 permits.
last_summary caches what the other system said. Cached foreign text, not modelled work.
last_status is the other system's word, cached for display and never this Case's state (CAS-04).
case_satisfaction.rating is a resident's judgement of handling, not a monetary or work-execution fact.

keptVerbatim.money: Inherited unchanged. ADR-020 D1 is the same boundary as ADR-011 D1 one layer out: no cost, price, amount, invoice or charge on a Case.
keptVerbatim.secrets: Inherited unchanged. A credential in any schema is a defect regardless of which module it is in; there is no argument for narrowing it here.

dropped.instrument: DROPPED, and this is the only whole group removed. lease/deed/mortgagee/landregistry are TENANCY instruments — the resident.interest boundary. A Case about a leaking pipe has no reason to name them, but neither would a false positive here be catching an ADR-020 violation: it would be catching an ADR-011 one, in a schema ADR-011's own scan does not cover. Keeping it would make this list assert a boundary it is not the guard for, and a check that fails for another rule's reason teaches people to widen the allowlist. Terms dropped: lease, leasereference, tenancyagreement, breakclause, renewal, renewaloption, rentreview, agent, agentname, deed, titledeed, landregistry, memorial, chargee, mortgagee, assignment

invertedIn.work_execution: ADDED — the group this list exists for. Nothing equivalent appears in any earlier denylist because no earlier module consumed an external work order. This is the ADR-020 D1 boundary made mechanical.
invertedIn.monetary_type: ADDED, and it changes the SCAN, not just the terms: a monetary column can hide behind an innocent name and a numeric type. The interest list scanned names only and did not need this.

modified.allowedExceptions: The interest list allowed source/reference/unit/company. `reference` is kept and joined by summary, status and rating — all four are things PEMO legitimately holds ABOUT foreign work or about a resident's judgement, rather than the work itself. source/unit/company are dropped as unused here: an exception nothing needs is an unexplained hole.
